reuse.why: The API and existing consumers use getScheduledAmount, which also reuses the existing getApproxNumberThreshold tolerance helper.

duplication.why: Expected-amount selection remains centralized without introducing duplicate arithmetic or caller-specific implementations.

placement.why: Schedule policy stays in shared/schedules, tolerance stays in shared/rules, and the API exposes the computed result at its response boundary.

scope.why: The changes focus on the requested policy, its consumers, and supporting API types, tests, documentation, and release notes.

maintainability.why: The shared implementation remains compact and removes obsolete rounding configuration, although the API documentation retains an outdated description of the policy.

bypasses_abstraction.where: The API and updated consumers delegate expected-amount decisions to getScheduledAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: No renamed or reshaped copies of expected-amount or tolerance logic are introduced.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount adds the op parameter and an isapprox conditional; both represent requested domain variation, while the obsolete rangeRounding parameter is removed.
